arm: D-1c directional / resolved-Coulomb / rope arm on the K-092 seed set

scope.licence: already-seen set, excluded from D-12 by construction; everything else is a deterministic field on a uniform time grid at those same sites. D-7 remains STRUCK.

does_not_score_the_frozen_prediction: The frozen scalar is the app's vertical body-tide displacement, which has NO Shida number and NO horizontal component and therefore cannot express a bearing. This arm necessarily uses engine/tidal_tensor.py, a DIFFERENT scalar, and therefore tests a DIFFERENT claim from D-12/D-13. Stated here rather than discovered later.
not_evidence: A null here bounds the largest un-mined degree of freedom cheaply. A hit here is NOT a finding, because the set was selected by having been looked at; it would be a reason to build the lattice and pay for it under section P7-24, and nothing more.

declaration.multiplicity: max-statistic calibration over the whole battery, and over the whole geometry grid for the secondary; dependence handled implicitly because the null replicates carry it; Phipson-Smyth exact p with +1 top and bottom
declaration.scope_flags: ALL OF sitetide.SCOPE_FLAGS, PLUS: (1) FREE-SURFACE PLANE STRESS -- the stress tensor is formed under sigma_rr = sigma_rN = sigma_rE = 0, exact at the free surface and approximate at hypocentral depth; no absolute Coulomb amplitude from this module is a measurement, only a detection statistic against an identically-constructed null. (2) THE FAULT MECHANISM IS A DECLARED ASSUMPTION, not a datum -- sitetide's 'no receiver mechanism, so no Coulomb resolution' flag is NOT lifted, it is made explicit so the assumption can be gridded and priced. (3) The absent ocean load is DIRECTIONAL and largest at coastal subduction sites, so it is a worse omission for a bearing statistic than for a scalar one.
declaration.bearing_convention: Bearings are AZIMUTHS IN DEGREES CLOCKWISE FROM NORTH, in [0, 180) because a principal axis is an undirected line and 'pull along 030' and 'pull along 210' are the same state. Any circular statistic on a bearing is therefore an AXIAL statistic on a pi-periodic variable and must be doubled before a standard circular test is applied -- see axial_to_circular().

secondary_grid_note: The grid's maximum is NOT calibrated against a grid-wide null in this run: each cell carries its own max-statistic p, but the maximum ACROSS 45 cells needs a null in which the whole grid is re-scanned per replicate. That is a declared limitation of this arm, not an oversight; the primary geometry is the calibrated result and the grid is reported as a sensitivity display only.

dated_correction_20260822.what_is_retracted: The D-1c commit message (1f445c7) and the supervisor's report described this arm's CFS mid-concentration as 'the opposite direction from the scalar axis' and as a second, independent marginal signal. THAT IS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED.
dated_correction_20260822.why: corr(areal-strain scalar, CFS thrust rake 90) = -0.9506, measured. Low CFS is therefore HIGH scalar, so this arm's CFS_TROUGH deficit (z -3.08) and D-1's CREST deficit (z -2.54) are THE SAME OBSERVATION expressed in anti-correlated coordinates. This arm is NOT independent evidence and it inherits every one of the five reasons P7-25(2) ruled the crest deficit NOT CLAIMABLE and NOT QUOTABLE.
dated_correction_20260822.the_friction_and_dip_grid_was_vacuous: At the declared free-surface plane stress (s_DD = s_rN = s_rE = 0) the fault normal's only surviving part is its horizontal component, giving sigma_n = sin^2(d) N(s+90) and, at rake 90, tau = -sin(d)cos(d) N(s+90), hence CFS = sin(d)(mu sin(d) - cos(d)) N(s+90). Both tractions are the SAME time function scaled by a geometry constant. VERIFIED NUMERICALLY: corr(CFS(250,20,0.4), N(340)) = -1.000000 and the maximum relative deviation from the closed form is 5.658e-16. Within each strike all 9 dip-by-friction cells have |corr| = 1.000000 with each other. THE 45-CELL GRID IS 5 DISTINCT STATISTICS, INDEXED BY STRIKE ALONE. Friction and dip are algebraically inert at the free surface and this arm did not test friction physics.
dated_correction_20260822.what_is_NOT_affected: The grid-wide max-statistic calibration is CONSERVATIVE, not wrong: calibrating over 45 cells that are really 5 makes the null maximum if anything too generous, so no false positive was manufactured. BEARING_R2 (z +1.43) and ROT_RATE (z -1.81) are the only two statistics that sampled near-orthogonal directions and both stand as reported; neither reached 2 sigma. The arm was not wrong, it was aimed at the wrong ~89 percent of the space.
dated_correction_20260822.assertions_added: engine/tests/test_tidal_tensor.py::test_free_surface_coulomb_is_a_scalar_multiple_of_the_fault_normal_bearing asserts the closed form across the whole declared grid, so any FUTURE mu-dependence is recognised as evidence that the vertical stress components have become non-zero (depth, or an ocean load) rather than as a finding about friction.
